questions.question: A raja and his wife founded a Mahila Mandal in a small Maharashtra town to advance Dalit women's right to education and employment. In which town was it based, and what was the royal family's surname?
questions.rationale: The paragraph is the only place in the corpus naming Phaltan and the Nimbalkar family as founders of this Mahila Mandal.

questions.question: One assessment of India's push toward AI-enabled digital transformation gives a five-year growth figure for the country's AI sector, plus how much private investment in it rose between 2016 and 2017. What was the five-year growth figure, and what were the 2016 and 2017 investment amounts?
questions.rationale: These three dollar figures appear together only in this paragraph's account of India's AI investment growth.

questions.question: A woman married at age nine in 1877 had been born a few years earlier under a different name. Her husband, a social reformer, was later imprisoned for seven months for defaming a British-appointed regent. What was her birth name, and in what year was he imprisoned?
questions.rationale: Only this paragraph gives her birth name, Ambu Phadke, alongside the 1883 imprisonment for defamation of a British-appointed regent.

questions.question: Arguing against a wholesale return to bygone Hindu social practices, a writer named a specific old custom that let a widow bear sons with her deceased husband's brother, and separately cited a ritual involving suspension from hooks as evidence of how brutal past practices had been. What was the custom called, and what was the hook ritual called?
questions.rationale: The Niyoga system and hook-swinging are named together only in this paragraph's list of discarded Hindu customs.

questions.question: An essay on rationalism quotes a historian of Greek thought crediting a particular ancient Greek system with turning the world's formation from a supernatural event into a natural one. Who was the historian quoted, and what was that system called?
questions.rationale: Cornford's name and the Milesian system appear together only in this quoted paragraph on the origins of rational naturalism.
